quotations.title: Noncritical Belyi Maps
quotations.author: Shinichi Mochizuki
quotations.exactquotation: Moreover, if X, S, and T are defined over a number field F, then \phi may be taken to be defined over F.
quotations.sourceparagraph: Theorem 2.5. (Belyi Maps Noncritical at Prescribed Points) Let X be a smooth, proper, connected curve over \overline{\mathbb{Q}} and S,T \subseteq X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) finite sets of \overline{\mathbb{Q}}-rational points such that S \cap T = \emptyset. Then there exists a morphism \phi : X \to \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} such that: (a) \phi is unramified over \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\backslash\{0,1,\infty\}; (b) \phi(S) \subseteq \{0,1,\infty\}; (c) we have \phi(T) \cap \{0,1,\infty\} = \emptyset. Moreover, if X, S, and T are defined over a number field F, then \phi may be taken to be defined over F.
quotations.contextual_support: Theorem context: smooth proper curves, finite disjoint algebraic point sets and number-field descent.
quotations.does_not_establish: This clause does not prove residue finiteness or identify the formal valuative Model carrier with the geometric curve.

quotations.title: Noncritical Belyi Maps
quotations.author: Shinichi Mochizuki
quotations.exactquotation: Since X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) is infinite, we may always adjoin to T extra points of X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) that do not lie in S;
quotations.sourceparagraph: Proof. Since X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) is infinite, we may always adjoin to T extra points of X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) that do not lie in S; in particular, we may assume, without loss of generality, that T has cardinality \geq 2g_X+1, where g_X is the genus of X. Write D \overset{\mathrm{def}}{=} \sum_{t\in T}[t] for the effective divisor on X obtained by taking the formal sum of the points in T, each with multiplicity one; denote the associated line bundle \mathcal{O}_X(D) by \mathcal{L} and the canonical bundle of X by \omega_X. Also, we shall write s_0 \in \Gamma(X,\mathcal{L}) for the section [uniquely determined up to a \overline{\mathbb{Q}}^{\times}-multiple] whose zero divisor is D. Thus, the degree \deg(\mathcal{L}) of \mathcal{L} is \geq 2g_X+1\geq 1. In particular, if x\in X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}), then \deg(\omega_X\otimes\mathcal{L}^{-1}(x))\leq(2g_X-2)-(2g_X+1)+1=-2 so \Gamma(X,\omega_X\otimes\mathcal{L}^{-1}(x))=0. Since, by Serre duality, \Gamma(X,\omega_X\otimes\mathcal{L}^{-1}(x)) is dual to H^1(X,\mathcal{L}(-x)), we thus conclude that H^1(X,\mathcal{L}(-x))=0. Now if we consider the long exact cohomology sequence associated to the exact sequence of coherent sheaves on X 0\to\mathcal{L}(-x)\to\mathcal{L}\to\mathcal{L}\otimes k(x)\to 0 [where k(x) is the residue field of X at x] we obtain an exact sequence \ldots\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})\to\mathcal{L}\otimes k(x)\to H^1(X,\mathcal{L}(-x))\to\ldots — i.e., we have a surjection \Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{L}\otimes k(x). Since \overline{\mathbb{Q}} is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L}) such that s_1(t)\ne0 for all t\in T. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections s_0, s_1 of \mathcal{L} has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism \psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} such that the pull-back by \psi of the unique [up to isomorphism] line bundle of degree 1 on \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} is isomorphic to \mathcal{L}; \psi maps every t\in T to the point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}. Moreover, since every point of the support of D has multiplicity one in D, \psi is unramified over the point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}; since no point of S lies in the support of D, this point “0” of \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} does not lie in the set \psi(S).
quotations.contextual_support: Infinite algebraic-point carrier and the enlargement of a finite point set before a sufficiently high degree construction.
quotations.does_not_establish: This is not a statement about rational points X(Q), finite fields, or finiteness of all algebraic points.

finite_dimensionality_coverage.what_p6_does_supply: Spaces of sections of a divisor line bundle on a smooth proper curve, negative-degree vanishing, Serre duality, and a surjective evaluation map to its residue-field fiber.
finite_dimensionality_coverage.permitted_claim: This page is a Mochizuki geometric-context citation for our independent Riemann/dimension layer.
finite_dimensionality_coverage.not_permitted_claim: Theorem 2.5 p.6 directly proves all of our Lean finite-dimensionality, kernel, basis-power, principal-degree-zero, or integer-supremum details.

recommended_short_english_source_notice: Shinichi Mochizuki, Noncritical Belyi Maps (May 2004), proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 6, https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Noncritical%20Belyi%20Maps.pdf . Mochizuki uses an actual effective divisor D=\sum_{t\in T}[t], its line bundle \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{O}_X(D), vanishing and evaluation into a residue-field fiber, and the infinitude of \overline{\mathbb{Q}} to choose a section nonzero at every point of T. This is geometric context for the independent Riemann/divisor/dimension adaptation. Exact Lean constructions and proofs are adapted from Belyi/CurveField/{Divisor,RiemannRochSpace,Riemann}.lean at 9ce4d3f793d3bc831f2fc7214b7dbad90ea012d8, the Belyi revision pinned by refer/iut; the Mochizuki passage does not state all of those formal details.
